purpose: Teach: 輸出入/顛末/参与/受け手/撤収/マージン/例示/売り出し

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、輸出入バランスを見直せ
lines.style: Clipped, authoritative. Even cadence, no softening. Command spoken as assumption of compliance, not request.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。前回のクレーム顛末を報告書にまとめました
lines.en: Yes. I've compiled the complaint follow-up into a report.
lines.style: Steady, professional. Slight pause before details — showing he's prepared. Formal register but not stiff. Eye contact level: measured.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、業界団体への参与人事を確定しろ
lines.en: Confirm the personnel for our industry association involvement.
lines.style: Clear and decisive. Each phrase lands with weight. No rush, no repetition. The voice of someone used to being obeyed.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。マーケティングは受け手の視点を大事にします
lines.en: Yes. Marketing will prioritize the customer's perspective in this approach.
lines.style: Respectful nod in the voice. Slightly more engaged than the previous affirmative — showing he understands the strategic point. Professional warmth underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 当社、不採算店舗の撤収を決断しろ
lines.en: Make the decision to close our unprofitable stores.
lines.style: Firm, final. The tone of someone making a hard call. No hedge, no softening particle. Pause weight before the command lands.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。新商品のマージンを再計算しました
lines.en: Yes. I've recalculated the margins on the new product line.
lines.style: Confirmation with substance. Slight lift at the end — indicating follow-through on an earlier directive. Capable, not celebratory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 提案書には事例を例示で示せ
lines.en: Use case examples in the proposal — concrete ones.
lines.style: Specific, almost curt. The correction of someone who knows what works. Expects the listener to understand immediately why this matters.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。新商品の売り出し時期を確定いたしました
lines.en: Yes. I've confirmed the launch timing for the new product.
lines.style: Clean closure. Steady, assured. A slight sense of completion in the pacing — the conversation's weight resolved. Professional satisfaction without overstatement.
